target_customer: Developers running fleets of coding agents across laptops, servers and sandboxes
problem: Long running coding agents die when a laptop closes or SSH drops, and developers cannot see which agent is blocked or done.
business_model: Open-source runtime; commercial monetization not stated (one source mentions commercial licenses for organizations that cannot use AGPL)
product_category: Agent runtime and terminal multiplexer for coding agents

founders.name: Can Celik
previous_startups: Built AI-assisted ultrasound technology (per YC page, startup not named)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led AI teams in fintech; employers and education not given.

competitors.name: Claude Squad
competitors.what: Terminal manager running coding agents in tmux and git worktrees

competitors.name: dmux and comux
competitors.what: CLI tools running multiple coding agents in parallel with tmux and git worktrees

competitors.name: Agent of Empires
competitors.what: Rust wrapper around tmux to manage agent sessions

technical_complexity.rationale: A persistent session server with agent state detection, SSH and mobile clients and a plugin API is solid systems work, though tmux style tools already existed.

defensibility.rationale: Apache licensed and easy to fork (many repos with the same name exist); the plugin marketplace and community are the only lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Agent vendors keep adding their own session and agent management features; no acquisition of herdr found as of 2026-11.

market_need_then: Multiple blogs in 2026 list tools for running parallel coding agents; the company reports 25k GitHub stars and 340k downloads four months after launch (company claim, one awesome list shows about 23k).

identity.visual_style: customizable themes and layouts, user mods showcased
identity.voice_and_tone: playful: No two Herdrs look alike

branding.brand_signature: Made for your agents. Remade by them.
branding.community_and_virality: Reviews and guides on several developer blogs (Thoughtworks Radar listing, Better Stack, others); company says its plugin marketplace passed 500 community plugins; many repositories under other owners share the name.

brand_strength.rationale: Herding metaphor with vowel dropped name, strong developer press for a one person team, but name is easily confused with forks and Herdr/herd tools.

outcome_analysis: herdr is a solo founder open-source project from Ankara that grew quickly with coding agent adoption, joined the Fall 2026 YC batch and announced a 6 million dollar Bessemer led seed on 2026-09-08. Growth came from open-source distribution and developer press. Risks are forks, agent vendors absorbing the feature and unclear monetization. No exit.
notes: Seed confirmed by company blog and an aggregator coverage. License is stated as Apache 2.0 on company pages but one search summary says AGPL for the main repo, unresolved. Star count is a company claim.
